name: run a tame walk from a known point and a wild walk from the target, with value-determined jumps, until they meet
mechanism: each walk jumps by an amount chosen from the current value alone, so once two walks land on a common point they coincide forever; start one from a known exponent, record its distance travelled, start the other from the unknown, and when the wild walk hits a point the tame one recorded, the two distances give the unknown

sources.ref: List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Pollard's kangaroo algorithm (also known as Pollard's lambda algorithm)' in section Computational mathematics / Computer algebra: an algorithm for solving the discrete logarithm problem

requires: the unknown known to lie in an interval
a jump function of the value alone
fails_when: the walks may miss; expected cost is the square root of the interval width
instances: Pollard's kangaroo algorithm (also known as Pollard's lambda algorithm)
